answer: Each agent's first paid voyage must be vouched by an established peer who stakes tokens on the newcomer's honesty. A sybil attacker needing a thousand identities must forge a thousand vouched histories, each costing real peer capital, because a stake-slash rule burns the voucher's deposit when a newcomer cheats. Reputation accrues slowly, like coral building a reef, so mass-produced fakes stay visibly shallow. Timber-solid: the ledger publishes every vouch, letting anyone audit whether an agent's reputation is rooted or rotten.
